Batch purchase, top-up and depth increase work as in\n * src/PostageStamp.sol, with the same events and views. The difference: no batch tree and no on-chain\n * expiry. See docs/ZK-SETTLEMENT.md, \"Postage accounting in the proof\".\n *\n * - A batch is expired when `normalisedBalance <= currentTotalOutPayment()`. Settlement then withdraws the proven amount with `withdraw(beneficiary, amount)`.\n * - `expiredBatchesExist()` and `expireLimited()` remain as no-ops, so current Bee versions (which call\n *   them before buying a batch) keep working.\n *\n * Buyers pay only for their own batch: no tree insert, no sweep of other batches.\n */\ncontract PostageStampZK is AccessControl, Pausable {\n    // ----------------------------- State variables ------------------------------\n\n    address public bzzToken;\n    uint8 public minimumBucketDepth;\n\n    bytes32 public immutable PRICE_ORACLE_ROLE;\n    bytes32 public immutable PAUSER_ROLE;\n    bytes32 public immutable REDISTRIBUTOR_ROLE;\n\n    mapping(bytes32 => Batch) public batches;\n\n    // Total out payment per chunk at `lastUpdatedBlock`, as in PostageStamp.\n    uint256 private totalOutPayment;\n    uint64 public lastPrice;\n    uint64 public minimumValidityBlocks = 17280;\n    uint64 public lastUpdatedBlock;\n\n    // Event log for the settlement proof. Entry i (1-based) is hashed into eventHash(i); the last\n    // EVENT_RING entries keep their hash and block so Settlement can check a prefix of the log.\n    uint256 public constant EVENT_RING = 256;\n    uint64 public eventCount;\n    bytes32[256] private eventHashRing;\n    uint64[256] private eventBlockRing;\n\n    uint8 public constant KIND_CREATE = 1;\n    uint8 public constant KIND_TOPUP = 2;\n    uint8 public constant KIND_DEPTH = 3;\n    uint8 public constant KIND_PRICE = 4;\n\n    // ----------------------------- Type declarations ------------------------------\n\n    struct Batch {\n        address owner;\n        uint8 depth;\n        uint8 bucketDepth;\n        bool immutableFlag;\n        uint256 normalisedBalance;\n        uint256 lastUpdatedBlockNumber;\n    }\n\n    struct ImportBatch {\n        bytes32 batchId;\n        address owner;\n        uint8 depth;\n        uint8 bucketDepth;\n        bool immutableFlag;\n        uint256 remainingBalance;\n    }\n\n    // ----------------------------- Events ------------------------------\n\n    // Same events as PostageStamp; Bee follows these.\n    event BatchCreated(\n        bytes32 indexed batchId,\n        uint256 totalAmount,\n        uint256 normalisedBalance,\n        address owner,\n        uint8 depth,\n        uint8 bucketDepth,\n        bool immutableFlag\n    );\n    event PotWithdrawn(address recipient, uint256 totalAmount);\n    event BatchTopUp(bytes32 indexed batchId, uint256 topupAmount, uint256 normalisedBalance);\n    event BatchDepthIncrease(bytes32 indexed batchId, uint8 newDepth, uint256 normalisedBalance);\n    event PriceUpdate(uint256 price);\n    event CopyBatchFailed(uint index, bytes32 batchId);\n\n    /**\n     * @dev One entry of the event log, with exactly the fields that are hashed:\n     * hash_i = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(hash_{i-1}, kind, batchId, owner, depth, bucketDepth, value,\n     * outpayment, blockNumber)). `value` is the batch's new normalisedBalance, or the new price for\n     * KIND_PRICE. `outpayment` is currentTotalOutPayment() after the change.\n     */\n    event PostageLog(\n        uint64 indexed index,\n        uint8 kind,\n        bytes32 batchId,\n        address owner,\n        uint8 depth,\n        uint8 bucketDepth,\n        uint256 value,\n        uint256 outpayment,\n        uint64 blockNumber\n error TransferFailed();\n    error ZeroBalance();\n    error AdministratorOnly();\n    error BatchDoesNotExist();\n    error BatchExpired();\n    error BatchTooSmall();\n    error NotBatchOwner();\n ------------------------------\n\n    constructor(address _bzzToken, uint8 _minimumBucketDepth) {\n        bzzToken = _bzzToken;\n        minimumBucketDepth = _minimumBucketDepth;\n Same rules and event as PostageStamp.createBatch.\n     */\n    function createBatch(\n        address _owner,\n        uint256 _initialBalancePerChunk,\n        uint8 _depth,\n        uint8 _bucketDepth,\n        bytes32 _nonce,\n        bool _immutable\n    ) external whenNotPaused returns (bytes32) {\n        if (_owner == address(0)) {\n            revert ZeroAddress();\n        }\n        if (_bucketDepth == 0 || _bucketDepth < minimumBucketDepth || _bucketDepth >= _depth) {\n            revert InvalidDepth();\n        }\n\n        bytes32 batchId = keccak256(abi.encode(msg.sender, _nonce));\n        if (batches[batchId].owner != address(0)) {\n            revert BatchExists();\n        }\n        if (_initialBalancePerChunk < minimumInitialBalancePerChunk()) {\n            revert InsufficientBalance();\n        }\n\n        uint256 totalAmount = _initialBalancePerChunk * (1 << _depth);\n        if (!ERC20(bzzToken).transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), totalAmount)) {\n            revert TransferFailed();\n        }\n\n        _storeBatch(batchId, _owner, _depth, _bucketDepth, _immutable, _initialBalancePerChunk, totalAmount);\n        return batchId;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Admin migration of a batch, as PostageStamp.copyBatch. Same rules and event as PostageStamp.topUp.\n     */\n    function topUp(bytes32 _batchId, uint256 _topupAmountPerChunk) external whenNotPaused {\n        Batch memory batch = batches[_batchId];\n\n        if (batch.owner == address(0)) {\n            revert BatchDoesNotExist();\n        }\n        if (batch.normalisedBalance <= currentTotalOutPayment()) {\n            revert BatchExpired();\n        }\n        if (batch.depth <= minimumBucketDepth) {\n            revert BatchTooSmall();\n        }\n        if (remainingBalance(_batchId) + (_topupAmountPerChunk) < minimumInitialBalancePerChunk()) {\n            revert InsufficientBalance();\n        }\n\n        uint256 totalAmount = _topupAmountPerChunk * (1 << batch.depth);\n        if (!ERC20(bzzToken).transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), totalAmount)) {\n            revert TransferFailed();\n        }\n\n        batch.normalisedBalance = batch.normalisedBalance + (_topupAmountPerChunk);\n        batches[_batchId].normalisedBalance = batch.normalisedBalance;\n\n        _log(KIND_TOPUP, _batchId, batch.owner, batch.depth, batch.bucketDepth, batch.normalisedBalance);\n        emit BatchTopUp(_batchId, totalAmount, batch.normalisedBalance);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Increase the depth of a batch. Same rules and event as PostageStamp.increaseDepth.\n     */\n    function increaseDepth(bytes32 _batchId, uint8 _newDepth) external whenNotPaused {\n        Batch memory batch = batches[_batchId];\n\n        if (batch.owner != msg.sender) {\n            revert NotBatchOwner();\n        }\n        if (!(minimumBucketDepth < _newDepth && batch.depth < _newDepth)) {\n            revert DepthNotIncreasing();\n        }\n        if (batch.normalisedBalance <= currentTotalOutPayment()) {\n            revert BatchExpired();\n        }\n\n        uint8 depthChange = _newDepth - batch.depth;\n        uint256 newRemainingBalance = remainingBalance(_batchId) / (1 << depthChange);\n        if (newRemainingBalance < minimumInitialBalancePerChunk()) {\n            revert InsufficientBalance();\n        }\n\n        batch.normalisedBalance = currentTotalOutPayment() + newRemainingBalance;\n        batches[_batchId].depth = _newDepth;\n        batches[_batchId].lastUpdatedBlockNumber = block.number;\n        batches[_batchId].normalisedBalance = batch.normalisedBalance;\n\n        _log(KIND_DEPTH, _batchId, batch.owner, _newDepth, batch.bucketDepth, batch.normalisedBalance);\n        emit BatchDepthIncrease(_batchId, _newDepth, batch.normalisedBalance);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Set the price. Paused(address).details: Emitted when the pause is triggered by `account`.

PostageLog(uint64,uint8,bytes32,address,.details: One entry of the event log, with exactly the fields that are hashed: hash_i = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(hash_{i-1}, kind, batchId, owner, depth, bucketDepth, value, outpayment, blockNumber)). `value` is the batch's new normalisedBalance, or the new price for KIND_PRICE. `outpayment` is currentTotalOutPayment() after the change.

RoleGranted(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is granted `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call, an admin role bearer except when using {AccessControl-_setupRole}.

RoleRevoked(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is revoked `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call:   - if using `revokeRole`, it is the admin role bearer   - if using `renounceRole`, it is the role bearer (i.e. `account`)

Unpaused(address).details: Emitted when the pause is lifted by `account`.

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleGranted} event.

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been revoked `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `account`. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

userdoc.notice: PostageStamp for ZK settlement. Batch purchase, top-up and depth increase work as in src/PostageStamp.sol, with the same events and views. The difference: no batch tree and no on-chain expiry. See docs/ZK-SETTLEMENT.md, "Postage accounting in the proof". - A batch is expired when `normalisedBalance <= currentTotalOutPayment()`. Every reader (this contract,   Bee, the proof) evaluates that directly. Nothing is removed. - The pot is not computed here. Every change that affects it (batch created, copied, topped up,   deepened, price changed) is appended to an event log: a hash chain plus a `PostageLog` event. The   settlement proof replays the log, expires batches in order and computes the pot, exactly as   `expireLimited` did. Settlement then withdraws the proven amount with `withdraw(beneficiary, amount)`. - `expiredBatchesExist()` and `expireLimited()` remain as no-ops, so current Bee versions (which call   them before buying a batch) keep working. Buyers pay only for their own batch: no tree insert, no sweep of other batches.
